description: We are a team of students from different backgrounds, united by one goal: to make a real change in Ethiopia’s agriculture. With knowledge in engineering and IT, we use NASA Space Apps data, such as satellite data on rainfall and soil moisture, to build solutions that help farmers make better decisions. Together, we bring fresh perspectives to make farming easier, smarter, and more rewarding.
summary:
Nebula – Smart Farming and Crop Health Monitoring Platform

Nebula is a smart farming platform developed to help Ethiopian farmers make informed, data-driven agricultural decisions. It addresses challenges such as unpredictable weather, limited access to agricultural information, and inadequate crop monitoring, which often leave farmers relying heavily on traditional farming practices.

We developed a farmer-friendly web platform that brings together crop health monitoring, environmental data, and location-based farm information. It tracks important conditions such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity, wind speed, and rainfall to help identify potential crop risks. Nebula also provides actionable farming recommendations and supports multilingual communication through Amharic SMS recommendations, making agricultural information more accessible to local communities.

By connecting environmental information with practical farming guidance, Nebula aims to help farmers respond to changing conditions, protect crop productivity, and make better farming decisions. It also provides a foundation for agricultural institutions and government bodies to better support farming communities through data-driven insights.
details:
NEBULA

Satellite-Powered Agricultural Intelligence for Ethiopian Farmers

1. What It Does and How It Works

Nebula is a farm companion designed for Ethiopian wheat and coffee (buna) farmers. It transforms NASA Earth observation data into practical agricultural guidance, delivered through a website and SMS in the farmer's own language (Amharic and Afaan Oromoo).

Farmers can register their farms and crops and access a personal dashboard containing:

  • Crop health and vegetation condition insights.
  • Weather and environmental conditions.
  • Soil moisture information.
  • Rainfall charts and historical trends.
  • Early warnings for false rainfall onset.
  • Planting information to support informed agricultural decisions.

Nebula also provides a secure administrative portal for authorized Ministry of Agriculture personnel to select NASA datasets, geographical areas, and date ranges and retrieve environmental information.

The data processing workflow consists of four steps:

  1. Dataset selection: An authorized user selects a dataset, geographical area, and date range.
  2. Data retrieval and processing: The backend securely retrieves and processes the selected dataset.
  3. Crop condition assessment: A defined assessment method evaluates environmental conditions and estimates crop health.
  4. Information delivery: Results are made available through the farmer's website dashboard or SMS.

Every dataset retrieval is labeled with one of four statuses: New, Cached, Unavailable, or Failed. This ensures users can distinguish newly retrieved information from cached data and unsuccessful retrieval attempts.

2. Authentication and Authorization

Nebula implements an authentication and authorization system with two primary roles:

  • Moderator
  • Farmer

Role-based access control ensures that users can only access the functionality permitted by their roles.

Farmer Registration

Nebula supports two farmer registration methods.

A. Moderator-Assisted Registration

Moderators can register farmers through a dedicated registration form.

The form collects:

  • First Name
  • Father Name
  • Fayda ID
  • Password
  • Area

After registration, the moderator can send the farmer an SMS containing relevant planting information.

B. Self-Registration

Farmers who can independently access and use the website can register through the landing page.

This provides an alternative for farmers who do not require moderator assistance.

Role-Based Access

Moderators:

  • Register farmers.
  • Access moderator-specific administrative functions.
  • Initiate and send SMS messages to farmers.

Farmers:

  • Access their personal dashboards.
  • View crop health information.
  • Monitor rainfall, humidity, and soil moisture.
  • Receive agricultural guidance and warnings.

3. SMS Communication and Planting Guidance

Nebula supports farmers who have limited or no internet connectivity through SMS communication.

Moderators send SMS messages containing essential environmental information relevant to planting decisions.

The SMS messages include:

  • Humidity: Atmospheric humidity information.
  • Soil Moisture: Available soil moisture information.
  • Rainfall: Observed or estimated rainfall information.

This allows farmers to receive useful agricultural information even when they do not have smartphones or internet access.

Afro Messages Integration

Nebula uses the Afro Messages Beta Program for SMS integration.

The backend handles SMS API requests, while API credentials are configured through environment variables.

The following environment variables are required:

AFRO_API_TOKEN=
AFRO_IDENTIFIER_ID=

For development and testing, individual testers can replace these values with their own Afro Messages credentials.

This allows testers to independently configure and test SMS delivery without modifying the application's source code.

Security practices include:

  • Keeping API credentials in environment variables.
  • Excluding .env files from version control.
  • Providing an .env.example file with empty placeholders.
  • Never exposing SMS credentials in frontend code.
  • Handling SMS requests exclusively through the backend.

4. Benefits

Many Ethiopian farmers primarily rely on traditional farming practices and have limited access to reliable weather information and agricultural decision-support services.

Existing digital agricultural tools often face adoption challenges because of:

  • Limited internet connectivity.
  • Insufficient local-language support.
  • Limited access to environmental and agricultural data.
  • Dependence on smartphones and internet-based applications.

Nebula addresses these challenges by combining satellite-based environmental information, a web dashboard, and SMS communication.

Its SMS functionality makes essential agricultural information accessible even to farmers using basic mobile phones.

5. Intended Impact

Nebula aims to promote data-informed agricultural decisions, improve crop yields, and strengthen harvest resilience among Ethiopian wheat and coffee farmers.

Initial Pilot Areas

  • Arsi: Wheat farming.
  • Bale: Wheat farming.
  • Jimma: Coffee farming.

The platform is designed to expand beyond these initial pilot areas to support other agricultural regions and crops across Ethiopia.

Since Nebula relies on a website, backend infrastructure, satellite datasets, and SMS communication rather than specialized farmer hardware, its architecture can support expansion to larger farming communities.

Future Development

Planned improvements include:

  • Integration of additional NASA datasets.
  • Access to more historical environmental data.
  • Support for additional Ethiopian local languages.
  • More detailed farm-level environmental analysis.
  • Validation and refinement of crop-health assessment methods with agricultural experts.
  • Further improvements to false rainfall onset prediction.

6. Tools and Data Used

NASA Earth Observation Datasets

SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive)

  • Level 3 and Level 4 datasets.
  • Used for soil moisture information.

GPM IMERG (Global Precipitation Measurement)

  • Used for satellite-based rainfall estimates.

NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources)

  • Used for temperature, humidity, wind, and solar radiation information.

MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer)

  • Used for vegetation greenness and crop condition monitoring.

SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission)

  • Used for elevation and terrain information.

Complementary Open Datasets

Nebula also uses complementary open datasets to enrich its environmental analysis:

  • CHIRPS.
  • ERA5-Land.
  • Sentinel-2.
  • SoilGrids.
  • ESA WorldCover.

NASA datasets are clearly distinguished from complementary non-NASA datasets to maintain transparency about data sources.

7. Creativity and Innovation

Nebula brings satellite-based agricultural intelligence to farmers who may not have internet access, delivering information in their own languages.

Its design considers Ethiopia's agricultural seasons:

  • Kiremt.
